text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple p95 latency SLO breaches detected across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Smart routing layer triggered automated reroutes three times in the last 8m. Potential routing oscillation impacting request success rate. Auto-pageing oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Paging alex and priya.

alex: Looking now — seeing p95 jump to ~2.3s in us-east-1, then routing policy moved traffic to eu-west-1 which then spiked to ~2.1s and traffic flipped back. Looks like a feedback loop.

priya: I can confirm. The routing controller's cooldown was set to 30s and p95 threshold is 1000ms. With our bursty traffic, it keeps hitting and flipping.

martin: Is this the new fallback-by-region policy we rolled last week? Could be using a less-performant model variant in eu-west-1.

alex: Yes — policy name `fallback-region-pref` — when p95 > 1000 it routes 50% to secondary region and 50% stays. Secondary had older model v1.3-quant that has slower initialization under cold KV cache. That's increasing p95.

emily: Customer impact: We're seeing elevated tail latencies for a small subset of production calls (mainly long-context generation requests). Error rates stable but perceived slowness reported by a few internal customers. We should mark partial impact on status page if we don't have a quick mitigation.

oncall-sre: Triage plan: 1) Stop policy-driven reroutes to secondary region (temp disable), 2) Pin routing to primary region for affected routes, 3) If needed, revert routing policy config. Who can flip?

priya: I can disable the `fallback-region-pref` policy in the control plane now. Command: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/policies/fallback-region-pref/disable -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'`

ops-bot: Executing policy disable as requested by priya.

ops-bot: Done — policy `fallback-region-pref` disabled. Routing controller acknowledges config version 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z.

alex: Checking metrics after disabling — p95 in eu-west-1 dropped to baseline ~750ms, us-east-1 p95 stabilized at ~980ms. No new flips observed in the last 2m.

oncall-sre: Good. Now we'll pin affected routes to primary region and increase cooldown / raise p95 threshold for the routing controller to avoid thrash while we investigate. Priya, can you apply a temp config?

priya: Applying patch:
```yaml
routing_controller:
  p95_trigger_ms: 1400
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  max_reroutes_per_10m: 1
```

ops-bot: Patch applied to control plane (versioned as 2026-03-15T14:15:10Z).

alex: Observability note: we've instrumented an additional metric `routing.reroute_count{route,region}` to correlate with p95 spikes. Will chart and share.

martin: Root cause hypothesis: secondary region's model variant v1.3-quant has poor cold-KV performance and when it receives a sudden shift of request mix it spikes p95 which triggers the primary to send it more traffic, creating a rebound. Also cooldown too short and threshold too sensitive.

karen-pm: From product side — impacted customers likely using long-context generation. Emily, please draft a short status update. Mention partial latency impact and that we've applied mitigations (disabled fallback policy, increased cooldown).

emily: Drafting status: "We are investigating increased latency for some text-generation requests. Engineers have applied a temporary routing configuration to stabilize traffic and are investigating model variant performance in secondary regions. No request failures observed; customers may see higher response times for certain long-context calls." Will post in 5m.

oncall-sre: Next actions: - Run replay tests to reproduce cold-KV spike on v1.3-quant (martin + alex) - Evaluate promoting a better quantized variant or warm KV cache before allowing region-fallback (martin) - Add automatic cooldown backoff and require sustained breach window (alex) - Postmortem and configuration guardrails (owners assigned)

martin: Starting replay now using production traces (small-scale). If we reproduce, I'll prepare a fix: either warm workers on secondary or change fallback policy to failover-by-model-compatibility rather than region-first.

priya: Also let's add a short-term circuit: block reroutes if reroute_count > 1 within 10m for same route. That should break loops.

oncall-sre: Good call. We'll keep this thread open for updates and declare incident severity once we have customer impact quantified. For now, assign Severity: S3 (partial degradation).

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1851234567 | Severity S3 | Owner: oncall-sre | Status: Mitigating

emily: Status page updated: "Partial latency degradation for some generation requests in US and EU regions. Mitigations applied. Engineers investigating."

karen-pm: Noting customer top 5 contracts + support channels — we'll notify any paying customers who reported issues.

alex: Update: replays show v1.3-quant p95 goes >2s on first 20 cold calls, stabilizes after warmup. Suggest we either pre-warm caches or avoid sending traffic until warm.

martin: Filed follow-up: create routing guard that checks model warm state and only routes to model variants with warm_kv == true OR route at 10% ramp. Tagging infra+ml for rollout.

oncall-sre: Great. I'll keep monitoring. If p95 stays <1100ms for 20m we can move to Post-Incident Review.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Monitoring configured: alert cooldown extended, reroute suppression rule in place.

emily: I'll prepare the incident summary and notify customer success.

priya: Added config revert plan in runbook in case unexpected side-effects observed.

oncall-sre: Thanks everyone. Leaving notes here for the PIR.

[end of thread]
